Growth Mixture Model with Time-Varying Covariates

Source: R/time-varying-covariates.R
gmm_survey_tvc.Rd

Extends gmm_survey with comprehensive support for time-varying covariates (TVCs). TVCs can have direct effects on outcomes, indirect effects on growth parameters, and can interact with latent class membership.

Usage

gmm_survey_tvc(
  data,
  id,
  time,
  outcome,
  n_classes,
  tvc,
  growth_model = "linear",
  strata = NULL,
  cluster = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  tvc_effects = c("direct", "indirect", "both", "interaction"),
  tvc_lag = 0,
  center_tvc = TRUE,
  tvc_by_class = FALSE,
  starts = 500,
  cores = parallel::detectCores() - 1,
  convergence_threshold = 1e-06,
  max_iterations = 1000,
  seed = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

Data frame in long format containing repeated measurements

id

Character string specifying the individual ID variable name

time

Character string specifying the time variable name

outcome

Character string specifying the outcome variable name

n_classes

Integer number of latent classes (default: 2)

tvc

Formula specifying time-varying covariates. Variables must vary within individuals over time (e.g., ~ ses + parental_monitoring)

growth_model

Character string specifying growth model type: "linear" (default), "quadratic", "nonlinear", or "free_basis"

strata

Character string specifying stratification variable (optional)

cluster

Character string specifying cluster/PSU variable (optional)

weights

Character string specifying sampling weights variable (optional)

covariates

Character vector of time-varying covariate names (not yet implemented)

tvc_effects

Character string specifying how TVCs affect the model:

"direct"

TVCs directly predict outcome at each time point (default)

"indirect"

TVCs affect growth parameters (slopes)

"both"

Both direct and indirect effects

"interaction"

TVCs moderate class-specific trajectories

tvc_lag

Integer specifying lag for TVCs (0 = contemporaneous, 1 = lagged once, etc.)

center_tvc

Logical; center time-varying covariates? (default = TRUE)

tvc_by_class

Logical; allow TVC effects to differ by class? (default = FALSE)

starts

Integer number of random starts (default: 500)

cores

Integer number of CPU cores for parallel processing (default: 1)

convergence_threshold

Numeric convergence criterion for EM algorithm (default: 1e-6)

max_iterations

Integer maximum number of EM iterations (default: 1000)

seed

Integer random seed for reproducibility (optional)

verbose

Logical, print progress messages? (default: TRUE)

Value

An S4 object of class SurveyMixrTVC (extends SurveyMixr) with additional slots:

tvc_effects

Data frame with TVC effect estimates for each class

tvc_formula

Formula specifying time-varying covariates

tvc_type

Type of TVC effects modeled

tvc_centered_values

Centered covariate values used in estimation

Details

**Model Specifications:**

**1. Direct Effects Model:** $$Y_{it} = \beta_{0k} + \beta_{1k} t + \gamma_k X_{it} + \epsilon_{it}$$

where \(X_{it}\) is the time-varying covariate and \(\gamma_k\) is its class-specific effect on the outcome.

**2. Indirect Effects Model:** $$Y_{it} = \beta_{0k} + (\beta_{1k} + \delta_k \bar{X}_i) t + \epsilon_{it}$$

where \(\bar{X}_i\) is the individual mean of the TVC and \(\delta_k\) represents how the TVC affects the growth rate.

**3. Both Effects Model:** $$Y_{it} = \beta_{0k} + (\beta_{1k} + \delta_k \bar{X}_i) t + \gamma_k (X_{it} - \bar{X}_i) + \epsilon_{it}$$

This separates between-person effects (\(\delta_k\)) from within-person effects (\(\gamma_k\)).

**4. Interaction Model:** $$Y_{it} = \beta_{0k} + \beta_{1k} t + \gamma_k X_{it} + \lambda_k (t \times X_{it}) + \epsilon_{it}$$

where \(\lambda_k\) captures how the TVC moderates the trajectory slope.

**Time-Varying vs Time-Invariant:**

- **Time-invariant**: Constant for each individual (e.g., sex, baseline SES) - **Time-varying**: Changes within individuals (e.g., parental monitoring, stress)

The function automatically detects which covariates are time-varying by checking for within-individual variance.

**Centering:**

When center_tvc = TRUE, covariates are centered at their grand mean. This improves interpretability and can aid convergence. For "both" effects, person-mean centering is used to separate within- and between-person effects.

**Lagged Effects:**

Set tvc_lag > 0 to examine lagged effects of TVCs: - tvc_lag = 1: Previous time point predicts current outcome - tvc_lag = 2: Two time points back predicts current outcome

References

Curran, P. J., & Bauer, D. J. (2011). The disaggregation of within-person and between-person effects in longitudinal models of change. *Annual Review of Psychology*, 62, 583-619.

Hoffman, L. (2015). *Longitudinal Analysis: Modeling Within-Person Fluctuation and Change*. New York: Routledge.

Wang, L. P., & Maxwell, S. E. (2015). On disaggregating between-person and within-person effects with longitudinal data using multilevel models. *Psychological Methods*, 20(1), 63-83.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Simulate data with covariates
set.seed(999)
sim_data <- simulate_gmm_survey(
  n_individuals = 200,
  n_times = 4,
  n_classes = 2,
  covariates = TRUE,
  design = "stratified_cluster",
  n_strata = 2,
  n_clusters = 20,
  seed = 999
)

# Direct effects: covariate directly predicts outcome
fit_direct <- gmm_survey_tvc(
  data = sim_data,
  id = "id",
  time = "time",
  outcome = "outcome",
  n_classes = 2,
  tvc = ~ baseline_risk,
  tvc_effects = "direct",
  starts = 20
)

# Both within- and between-person effects
fit_both <- gmm_survey_tvc(
  data = sim_data,
  id = "id",
  time = "time",
  outcome = "outcome",
  n_classes = 2,
  tvc = ~ baseline_risk,
  tvc_effects = "both",
  starts = 20
)

# Extract TVC effects
tvc_effects <- extract_tvc_effects(fit_both)
print(tvc_effects)
} # }
